policy: Every sample is a real page already stored in Polaris's raw_document table, and every sample names the exact document_id it was labelled from. The M10 mistake of reading 'the latest fetch of this URL' is not repeated: a site that later serves an empty body must not be able to change this dataset.

Labels are hand-judged from the URL and the page's own title and headings. They are not copied from the classifier's output; where the classifier disagrees, the sample fails and the disagreement is reported.
The labels describe what the page IS, not whether Polaris can extract it well. A scholarship detail page that happens to be hard to parse is still SCHOLARSHIP_DETAIL.

Ambiguous pages are labelled UNKNOWN rather than forced into a class. UNKNOWN/NEEDS_REVIEW is the honest answer and the classifier is expected to prefer it to a confident wrong call. No stored page in this dataset earned that label, which is a finding rather than a gap: every real page Polaris has captured declares its own intent somewhere.
Each sample records the evidence a reader needs to reproduce the label without opening the page.

samples.why: One named scheme, its own h1, its own deadline and its own eligibility. Nothing on the page describes a collection.
samples.note: The M10 golden corpus already asserts this page states 'Deadline 09 Dec 2025' and matches no canonical funding type.

samples.why: A named award with an eligibility list and an application section. 'Deadline: On going' is still one award, not a catalogue.
samples.note: A page with no fixed closing date is still a detail page; the absence of a deadline is an extraction problem, not a classification problem.

samples.why: The path ends in the award's own slug and the title is the award's name.
A plural name, but one award page with eligibility and how-to-apply sections — the plural is the award's own title.
One award, its own deadline, its own eligibility.
The last path segment is a collection word and the page links to many named awards. This is the page class M10 fed to the extractor by mistake.
samples.note: Used as the canonical 'follow this, do not extract this' sample.

samples.why: The title says 'An Overview' and the page lists awards at several degree levels. It describes a family of opportunities.
samples.note: Hard case: the page is the DAAD scholarship section, so every naïve signal says 'scholarship page'. Only the self-declared overview wording separates it from a detail page.

samples.why: Guidance about applying, not an award. It sits inside the scholarship section and uses the funding vocabulary throughout, which is exactly why it needs an explicit rule.
A funding-options index linking out to many named programmes.
The title is 'Frequently Asked Questions' and the headings are questions. The site is a scholarship foundation, so every funding term is present.
samples.note: This page is also a M10 negative sample: it must yield no scholarship name. M10 fixed the name; M11 stops the page being acquired as a candidate at all.

samples.why: 'FAQs on scholarships' — questions about the application process, not an award.
The last path segment is the singular 'scholarship' but the page lists the Fulbright Master's, Doctoral and Research schemes. Singular and plural both mean collection here.
samples.note: Hard case: the title is plural-funding and the page carries eligibility sections, so several detail signals fire at once.

samples.why: A fellowships category page whose own title is just the plural collection word.
One named award with its own eligibility and benefit sections.

A contact-and-navigation page whose headings are menu labels and whose body is 661 characters, but which links to 9 scholarship-labelled destinations. It is not an award, and it is not a page to extract from; it is a place to find other pages.
samples.note: LABEL REVISED. The first hand label here was UNKNOWN, on the reasoning that the page has no scholarship content of its own. That was wrong: it does link to 9 funding-labelled destinations, which is the definition of an index. The revision was made after seeing the classifier's answer, so it is disclosed rather than presented as an independent label — the reasoning above is checkable against the stored document, and the classification is unchanged in effect: this page must never be extracted as a scholarship. It is also the one remaining M10 name-accuracy miss ('About JASSO and other programs for Japanese students'), so M10 and M11 independently concluded that this page must not become a record.
